State values

Start the same policy from the same cell twice and you get different returns, because the policy and the ice are both random. The value of a state is the return you get from it on average. It scores a state under a given policy with a single number.

Policy:

The icy gridworld from Lesson 20, $\gamma = 0.9$. "Arrows" is Lesson 20's starting policy. Click a cell to start episodes from it. Each cell shows its average return so far and how many episodes made it.

The maths

The return from time $t$ is the discounted sum of the rewards that follow (Lesson 4):

$$\begin{aligned} G_t &= R_{t+1} + \gamma R_{t+2} + \gamma^2 R_{t+3} + \dots \\ &= \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \gamma^k R_{t+k+1} \end{aligned}$$

The state-value function of policy $\pi$ is the expected return when starting in $s$ and following $\pi$ from then on:

$$v_\pi(s) = \mathbb{E}_\pi\big[G_t \mid S_t = s\big]$$

$\mathbb{E}_\pi$ averages over everything random: the actions $\pi$ picks and the slips of the ice. A terminal state has $v_\pi = 0$, since no rewards follow it.

If $n$ episodes start in $s$ and return $G^{(1)}, \dots, G^{(n)}$, their average estimates the value:

$$V(s) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} G^{(i)} \;\longrightarrow\; v_\pi(s) \quad \text{as } n \to \infty$$

This is the law of large numbers again (Lesson 5). Its typical error is the standard error, where $\sigma$ is the standard deviation of the returns:

$$\text{SE} = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$$

Four times as many episodes halves the error. Returns here are spread widely (from about $-10$ to $+10$), so a few episodes give a rough answer. Lesson 35 builds a learning method on exactly this averaging.

A value is always of a policy. Switch policies above: the same cell gets a different number.
